<DOCUMENT>Regularly review event logs for login activity and privilege escalation to identify and respond to potential security threats Event logs provide insights into system activity including successful and failed login attempts and privilege escalation events Monitor system logs for configuration changes and errors Routinely monitor system logs to detect configuration changes system errors and unusual data connections that may indicate security or operational issues System logs contain information about general activity including configuration changes system errors workflows and inboundoutbound data connections Review transaction logs to detect malicious web activity Review transaction logs to identify unusual or malicious web activity as they provide records of all browserbased interactions with the ServiceNow instance Enable table auditing for complete record history</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>PROTECT White Paper Identity and access management Authentication Customer responsibility In the context of the Security Shared Responsibility Model customers have the responsibility of configuring their instance using supported authentication methods This configuration process may include setting up multiprovider single signon SSO with security assertion markup language SAML or OpenID connect OIDC enabling smartcard authentication such as personal identity verification PIV or common access card CAC for environments requiring high security utilizing OAuth and enforcing multifactor authentication MFA</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>Best practice prioritization Customers should to evaluate each best practice in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to determine applicability and evaluate potential risks Therefore they must work closely with security and compliance teams when identifying the best practices to address Customers should also work with all stakeholders to set the prioritization of each best practice ServiceNow stands ready to provide guidance and support once youve begun implementing these measures Work with your account teams or open a ServiceNow Supporthttpssupportservicenowcom case for more clarification Companies are expected to evaluate each best practice in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to determine applicability and evaluate potential risks November 2025 Release Zurich 5</DOCUMENT>

<DOCUMENT>If the infrastructure hosting the currently active instance experiences a disruption ServiceNow activates a failover process that transfers customer operations to the unaffected colocation facility In this model the targeted recovery point objective RPO and recovery time objective RTO durations are one and two hours respectively Backups The ServiceNow Advanced High Availability AHAhttps architecture is the primary means to restore service in the case of a disruption that could impact availability however ServiceNow also performs backups of each customers instances In specific scenarios using more traditional data backup and recovery mechanisms may be appropriate Backups are stored in the same colocation facilities where the data resides with production instances backed up in both colocation facilities in the pair Full directtodisk backups are performed every seven days and retained for a minimum of 14 days Differential backups are taken every 24 hours</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>It is recommended that customers limit the use of personal identities for executing unattended automations or integrations By implementing ServiceNow access policy restrictions to clearly separate these data flows organizations can better define and uphold policies aligned with their identity architecture Use security attributes when possible Customers should utilize applicable security attributes when possible Security attributes offer an alternative method for access control via role definitions Use security data filters when possible Security data filters enable access restriction to records based on a users role or other security attributerelated assertions Security data filters are applied before a query is executed and ensure only authorized users can view records regardless of how data is accessed Customers should explicitly enable security data filters for userfacing queries that are not using GlideRecordSecure</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>PROTECT White Paper Best practices Understand the ServiceNow Data Sharing Program Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to fully understand how anonymized data is shared with ServiceNow Confirm the intended data contribution strategy with appropriate stakeholders Customers of the Advanced AI and Data Products can opt out of sharing data Refer to the Data Sharing Programs and AI Model Improvement KB1648406 for details on how ServiceNow collects and uses customercontributed data to enhance AI models as per the productspecific terms Customers can opt out of anonymized data sharing within 30 days of downloading an AI app from the ServiceNow Store Data sharing for the Advanced AI and Data Products can be managed from the Now Assist Admin Console Evaluate and configure AI model options on the ServiceNow AI Platform</DOCUMENT>

<DOCUMENT>White Paper Introduction Video Security Best Practices for the ServiceNow AI Platform Document goal and structure This document provides a comprehensive overview of key considerations for securing a ServiceNow instance under the Shared Responsibility model where both the service provider and the customer share accountability for security and compliance Each section is structured around the categories of Governance Identify Protect Detect Respond and Recover which reflect the natural progression of effective management and response Within those sections best practices follow a crawl walk run order The focus of this guide is recommendations rather than detailed platform descriptions All stakeholders should review the white paper for full details This document is designed to be read alongside Securing the ServiceNow AI Platform which gives a holistic overview of the physical administrative and technical controls ServiceNow has in place to protect customer data</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>White Paper Best practices continued Understand Account recovery ACR capabilities When utilizing Single SignOn SSO ensure that at least one Account Recovery ACR administrator is registered prior to activation This precaution secures fallback access to critical systems should primary authentication methods become misconfigured or unavailable Thoroughly document all ACR procedures limit access strictly to authorized personnel and regularly audit ACR usage to uphold strong security standards Restrict local logins for interactive sessions to approved recovery users with MFA enabled and employ ACR solely as a recovery tool to maintain system integrity</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>Some ServiceNow products rely on thirdparty Original Equipment Manufacturers OEM services such as Azure OpenAI Collaborate with your stakeholders to determine whether your organization will use these cloudbased models If they do not meet your security or compliance requirements configure ServiceNow to fully opt out of options like Microsoft Azure OpenAI Google Gemini or Anthropic Claude on Amazon Web Services AWS Note Certain skills may restrict model provider selection based on functional or technical limitations These exceptions are described in Model Provider Support Matrix for Now Assist Skills and AI Agents KB2222333 which outlines supported skills and agents for both the Now LLM and thirdparty OEM LLMs Data processing in production</DOCUMENT>

<DOCUMENT>White Paper Best practices continued Enforce email authentication and domain restrictions Customers can control what domains and users are allowed to send email into their ServiceNow instance as well as what domains and users are valid email destinations using system address filters Collaborate with your security and IT teams to determine if you need to configure any of the following email controls ServiceNow provides Sender Policy Framework SPF records to identify email hosts that are approved to send as ServiceNow To use SPF services the customers email systems must be configured to accept mail from the ServiceNow email infrastructure ServiceNow recommends that customers consume the published ServiceNow SPF records dynamically rather than allowing by IP address When allowing by IP address it is important to note that the addresses may change</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>If the infrastructure hosting the currently active instance experiences a disruption ServiceNow activates a failover process that transfers customer operations to the unaffected colocation facility In this model the targeted recovery point objective RPO and recovery time objective RTO durations are one and two hours respectively Backups The ServiceNow Advanced High Availability AHAhttps architecture is the primary means to restore service in the case of a disruption that could impact availability however ServiceNow also performs backups of each customers instances In specific scenarios using more traditional data backup and recovery mechanisms may be appropriate Backups are stored in the same colocation facilities where the data resides with production instances backed up in both colocation facilities in the pair Full directtodisk backups are performed every seven days and retained for a minimum of 14 days Differential backups are taken every 24 hours</DOCUMENT>

White Paper Best practices continued Understand Account recovery ACR capabilities When utilizing Single SignOn SSO ensure that at least one Account Recovery ACR administrator is registered prior to activation This precaution secures fallback access to critical systems should primary authentication methods become misconfigured or unavailable Thoroughly document all ACR procedures limit access strictly to authorized personnel and regularly audit ACR usage to uphold strong security standards Restrict local logins for interactive sessions to approved recovery users with MFA enabled and employ ACR solely as a recovery tool to maintain system integrity

ServiceNow has separate business continuity plans and processes which are tested annually in place to ensure availability for the ServiceNow corporate organization and the services it relies on Advanced High Availability AHA architecture ServiceNow colocation facilities are arranged in regional pairs with all customer production data hosted in both colocation facilities simultaneously ServiceNow uses asynchronous database replication to keep these pairs in sync When performing maintenance or if an infrastructure component fails transfer between active and passive colocation facilities is executed as part of ServiceNow standard operating procedures This ensures that when AHA is needed to address an instance failure the transfer will be successful and service disruption minimized

Regularly review event logs for login activity and privilege escalation to identify and respond to potential security threats Event logs provide insights into system activity including successful and failed login attempts and privilege escalation events Monitor system logs for configuration changes and errors Routinely monitor system logs to detect configuration changes system errors and unusual data connections that may indicate security or operational issues System logs contain information about general activity including configuration changes system errors workflows and inboundoutbound data connections Review transaction logs to detect malicious web activity Review transaction logs to identify unusual or malicious web activity as they provide records of all browserbased interactions with the ServiceNow instance Enable table auditing for complete record history

White Paper Request that the support case be marked as a security case If a case being submitted involves confirmed compromise of customer information customers are able to request the case be flagged as a security case which limits the case visibility as needed Ensure that security cases are intentionally designated as such Customer visibility into a security case is limited to the submitter and any accounts designated on the cases watchlist Educate your security team on how to raise a case with ServiceNow Support Ensure that your security team or at a minimum the designated security contact in Security Contacts on ServiceNow Support has documentation on how to create a support case via supportservicenowcom in the event they need to report an incident and cannot contact a member of the platform team Understand how to review logs for investigations

ServiceNow responsibility ServiceNow operates a Security Information and Event Management SIEM system to review and correlate logs from multiple network and infrastructure sources A Scheduled Security Operations Checklist is in place which includes daily reviews of Linux and Windows systems Network devices Intrusion Detection System IDS alerts Behavioral and identified issue logs Highrisk issues such as intrusion detection events trigger realtime alerts that are immediately sent to the Security Incident Response Team for review Network and infrastructure log events are retained for a minimum of 90 days Best practices Define a log monitoring strategy

ServiceNow has separate business continuity plans and processes which are tested annually in place to ensure availability for the ServiceNow corporate organization and the services it relies on Advanced High Availability AHA architecture ServiceNow colocation facilities are arranged in regional pairs with all customer production data hosted in both colocation facilities simultaneously ServiceNow uses asynchronous database replication to keep these pairs in sync When performing maintenance or if an infrastructure component fails transfer between active and passive colocation facilities is executed as part of ServiceNow standard operating procedures This ensures that when AHA is needed to address an instance failure the transfer will be successful and service disruption minimized

<DOCUMENT>White Paper Introduction Video Security Best Practices for the ServiceNow AI Platform Document goal and structure This document provides a comprehensive overview of key considerations for securing a ServiceNow instance under the Shared Responsibility model where both the service provider and the customer share accountability for security and compliance Each section is structured around the categories of Governance Identify Protect Detect Respond and Recover which reflect the natural progression of effective management and response Within those sections best practices follow a crawl walk run order The focus of this guide is recommendations rather than detailed platform descriptions All stakeholders should review the white paper for full details This document is designed to be read alongside Securing the ServiceNow AI Platform which gives a holistic overview of the physical administrative and technical controls ServiceNow has in place to protect customer data</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>Establish a formal procedure to identify relevant parties including compliance teams vendor risk assessment teams and security personnel who require access to CORE documentation for internal audits and vendor evaluations and provide them with the necessary portal access Periodically review the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal Establish a process involving relevant stakeholders to conduct regular reviews of CORE content and implement a method for collecting and addressing clarification questions following material review Use the completed questionnaires in the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal to support due diligence efforts</DOCUMENT>
